name: Singular
description: Singular is a mobile marketing analytics and attribution platform for campaign performance, cost aggregation, creative intelligence, fraud prevention, deep links, and data exports. Growth and marketing teams use it to unify acquisition data across apps, sites, and advertising partners.
agentUseSummary: Add a customer-generated Singular Reporting API key; agents can list a redacted bounded set of internal app-site references through one fixed Singular Links helper endpoint.

credentialRequirements.name: SINGULAR_API_KEY
credentialRequirements.label: Singular Reporting API key
credentialRequirements.helpText: Generate a dedicated Reporting API key. Relay encrypts it and sends it only in the Authorization header to api.singular.net.

capabilities.label: Read app-site references
capabilities.description: Read at most 25 internal app/app-site ID and platform references with names, public/bundle IDs, and URLs excluded.

approvalRequired.label: List Singular app-site references
approvalRequired.description: Return at most 25 validated internal app/app-site IDs and platform labels plus aggregate total/truncation state.

blocked.label: Access app identity or destinations
blocked.description: App names, bundle IDs, public/store IDs, store URLs, websites, domains, destinations, deep links, tracking links, aliases, and routing content remain blocked.

blocked.label: Access attribution, device, or reporting data
blocked.description: Users, devices, advertising IDs, IPs, locations, clicks, installs, events, campaigns, creatives, partners, revenue, cost, fraud, cohorts, reports, raw data, and exports remain blocked.

blocked.label: Create, write, or administer Singular
blocked.description: Link creation, apps, app sites, partners, domains, destinations, reports, events, callbacks, SDK/S2S ingestion, credentials, users, and administration remain blocked.

blocked.label: Use raw API or bulk access
blocked.description: SDK keys, arbitrary origins, paths, methods, headers, queries, bodies, dates, dimensions, metrics, filters, pagination, polling, retries, SDKs, browser sessions, bulk, and exports remain blocked.

approvalProfiles.label: Safe
approvalProfiles.description: The bounded app-site read requires approval; identity, link content, attribution, reports, writes, raw APIs, and bulk remain blocked.

approvalProfiles.label: Dangerously skip permissions
approvalProfiles.description: The same bounded read runs directly; key authority, fixed endpoint, redaction, caps, audits, and provider limits remain mandatory.

runtimeSupport.description: OpenClaw receives one fixed redacted Singular Links Get Apps wrapper.
Hermes receives the same fixed redacted Singular Links Get Apps wrapper.

providerSetup.blocker: Singular Links API access is a premium Enterprise/Commercial feature and requires an eligible customer account plus a current Reporting API key.
providerSetup.nextAction: A customer admin confirms Singular Links API entitlement, generates a dedicated Reporting API key, and completes a live read-only Get Apps acceptance check.

evidence.supports: Singular documents premium Singular Links API entitlement, Authorization-header Reporting API keys, fixed Get Apps endpoint/response fields, link read/create helpers, four GETs/minute, and link-creation quotas.

Singular documents API-key authentication plus broad reporting/filter/custom-dimension/cohort/conversion endpoints, report downloads, large row limits, and 401/403/404/429/500 errors; Relay blocks these surfaces.
Singular documents aggregated marketing reports, asynchronous report creation/status/download, dimensions, metrics, dates, campaigns, and connectors; Relay blocks reporting.
Singular documents separate SDK-key S2S event ingestion with device identifiers; Relay never accepts SDK keys or mounts ingestion.

securityNotes: The Reporting API key is encrypted and sent only in the Authorization header to https://api.singular.net.
Relay allowlists only GET /api/v1/singular_links/apps, rejects redirects, waits 30 seconds, caps responses at 1 MB, and respects the documented four-GETs-per-minute limit.

Output contains at most 25 validated internal app/app-site IDs and platform labels plus total/truncation state; names, public/bundle IDs, store URLs, links, destinations, identity, attribution, devices, partners, and reports are excluded.

Reports, filters, analytics, raw data, link creation/view detail, domains, partners, S2S/SDK ingestion, writes, administration, arbitrary inputs/endpoints, pagination, polling, retries, bulk, and exports remain blocked.
Provider setup, entitlement confirmation, key capture, permission assignment, and live acceptance remain customer/external steps.
